title: Maximal-dimension conjecture for constant-rank affine spaces of nilpotent matrices
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}-\{0\}$ and let $K$ be a field. Let $S$ be an affine subspace of $M(n\times n,K)$ such that every element of $S$ is nilpotent, and assume that each element of $S$ has rank equal to $r\geq 1$. **Constant-rank nilpotent dimension conjecture.** If $|K|$ is sufficiently large, then the maximal dimension $S$ can attain is

$$
\sum_{i=1}^r(n-1-i)=\frac{r}{2}(2n-r-3).
$$

This predicts the sharp dimension bound for affine spaces consisting of nilpotent matrices of fixed rank, extending the dimension question beyond the rank-one case and subject to a sufficiently large-field hypothesis.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06653

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
source_name: Simone Calamai and Elena Rubei, “On the dimension of affine subspaces of nilpotent matrices”, arXiv:2508.06653 (2025).
